findings.title: Sign up action is a clickable div, not keyboard accessible
findings.explanation: The primary submit action is a <div> with onClick and no role, tabIndex or key handler, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot reach or activate it. There is no real submit button in the form to provide the same action.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with <button type="submit">Sign up</button> and drop the onClick (the form's onSubmit handles it).

findings.title: Email input has only a placeholder, no label
findings.explanation: The input has no associated <label>, aria-label or aria-labelledby; a placeholder is not an accessible label. Screen-reader users cannot identify the field in the signup flow.
findings.suggested_fix: Add <label htmlFor="email">Email</label> and id="email" on the input (or an aria-label).

findings.title: Custom modal has no dialog semantics or focus management
findings.explanation: The modal is plain divs with no role="dialog", aria-modal, accessible name, initial focus, focus trap, or Escape-to-close, and no accessible dialog library is imported. Keyboard focus stays behind the overlay and users cannot dismiss it.
findings.suggested_fix: Use native <dialog> with showModal(), or an accessible library (Radix Dialog, Headless UI, React Aria); otherwise add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby, move focus in, trap it, close on Escape and restore focus on close.

findings.title: Image has no alt attribute
findings.explanation: The has no alt attribute at all, so screen readers may announce the file URL. Use alt="" if decorative.
findings.suggested_fix: Add alt text (e.g. an alt prop describing the user) or alt="" if the avatar is purely decorative.

limitations: Only the 3 source files in src/ were reviewed; no ESLint config was present so jsx-a11y status is unknown.
Color contrast, focus styles and actual screen-reader output cannot be verified from source.
Callers of these components were not present, so how they are used (e.g. Modal content) was not checked.
